summary: This note is a Wikipedia-sourced overview of the University of California, Irvine (UCI), a public research university in Irvine, California. It describes the school's place in the University of California system, its range of degree programs, and its research standing. It also covers its membership in the Association of American Universities and its informal reputation as a Public Ivy.
one_line: Overview of the University of California, Irvine, a public research university in Irvine, California, covering its degrees, research standing and reputation.
key_facts: The University of California, Irvine (UCI or UC Irvine) is a public research university located in Irvine, California.
UC Irvine is one of the 10 campuses in the University of California (UC) system.
UC Irvine offers 87 undergraduate degrees and 129 graduate and professional degrees.
The university is classified as a Research I university.
In 2017, UC Irvine had $361 million in research and development expenditures, according to the National Science Foundation.
UC Irvine became a member of the Association of American Universities in 1996.
UC Irvine is the youngest university to hold membership in the Association of American Universities.
UC Irvine is considered to be one of the "Public Ivies."
A Public Ivy is a publicly funded university thought to provide a quality of education comparable to that of the Ivy League.
